claims.statement: `packages/design-system` is the workspace package `@mcm/design-system`, a Material Design 3 token set plus Tamagui component library shared by the web and native builds of `frontend/mcm-app`. Its package exports are the barrel `.` → `index.ts` and `./tamagui.config` → `tamagui.config.ts`, and `expo`, `react` and `react-native` are declared as peer dependencies so the package never decides the app's framework versions.

Every semantic MD3 colour role is theme-split: `lightColors` and `darkColors` each map the tonal palettes to a distinct value per role (primary, secondary, tertiary, success, error, background/surface, surface1–surface5, outline, scrim, …), so one token resolves to an AA-passing colour on both the near-white light surface and the near-black dark surface.

The semantic colour roles exist only in the Tamagui themes, never also as colour tokens: the config flattens raw palette tones into tokens (`primaryP40`, …) but deliberately omits `...lightColors`, because Tamagui 3 resolves a bare name on a colour property token-first and theme second, so a duplicated light value would win inside the dark theme. Consumers read roles through `useTheme()` as `theme.<role>?.val`, and Tamagui 3 token/theme names carry no `$` sigil.

`success` is a first-class semantic colour role rather than an ad-hoc green literal, added so positive/verified state flows through the theme: positive text uses `theme.success?.val`, a filled verified banner uses `successContainer` with `onSuccessContainer`, and no consumer may use a green literal. The role exists in both colour maps and both themes, and the three required WCAG AA pairings are asserted in `components/success-token.test.tsx`.

The type scale is the MD3 step set `{11,12,14,16,18,22,24,28,32,36,45,57}`, with Outfit carrying display/headline/title and Inter carrying body/label. Both fonts declare only the faces 400/500/600/700, which is the rationale behind compliance rule R6: a `fontWeight` above 700 has no real face and is synthesized by the renderer.

`dark` is the recommended default theme, justified by the product being a movie-collection app where a home-theatre aesthetic is natural. The dark background is deliberately deeper than MD3's standard dark neutral — `#0F1117` instead of `#1A1C1E` — to evoke a cinema and make posters stand out.

Tamagui is pinned to one exact version (`3.0.18`) across both the design-system and mcm-app manifests, and `scripts/__tests__/tamagui-version-lockstep.guard.test.mjs` enforces that: no range specifiers, both manifests agreeing on the version, exactly one `@tamagui/core` and one `@tamagui/web` in the lock, no remaining `@tamagui/babel-plugin` in either manifest or `babel.config.js`, and every Tamagui update resolving to a single Renovate `tamagui` group so a partial lock refresh cannot split the set.

The app runs Tamagui runtime-only through `<TamaguiProvider>` with no Babel or Metro compiler plugin: Tamagui 3 removed the Babel plugin, and its replacement `@tamagui/metro-plugin` 3.0.x was measured and rejected because it lowered some web modules to static class names without emitting their CSS while saving no bytes. This is a measured decision, not a leftover, and re-adding a compiler incidentally is out of bounds.

Because Tamagui 3 removed config-level `defaultProps`, the body font and the theme's `onBackground` colour live on the design system's own `components/primitives/Text.tsx`. `components/text-defaults.test.tsx` pins that observable behaviour for both themes and fails if any source file outside `primitives/Text.tsx` imports `Text` from `@tamagui/core`, which would bypass the defaults (on native, leaving black text on the dark theme).

The app enforces design-system usage with a static scan run by its Jest unit suite, not a runtime check. The rules live in `frontend/mcm-app/tests/unit/design-system-compliance.test.ts` as one `it()` per rule (R1–R7), each asserting zero violations over `frontend/mcm-app/src/**` while excluding the `bff-server`/`bff-api`/`__mocks__`/`unit-tests` directories and test/spec files.

The scan engine lives in `frontend/mcm-app/tests/unit/ds-compliance-scan.ts`: it reads, neutralizes and brace-parses every source file once into a cached `ScanFile`, and the seven rule predicates iterate that cache. A failure reports `file:line — rule — snippet` per violation so a migration can be driven file by file, and the predicates are unit-tested in isolation on synthetic `ScanFile`s.

A deliberate deviation from a compliance rule requires BOTH a `// ds-exempt(R<n>): <reason>` marker on the flagged line or the immediately-preceding non-blank line (`ds-exempt(all)` exempts every rule) AND an entry in `specs/017-design-system-consistency/contracts/sanctioned-deviations.md`. The scan only sees the marker; the catalogue entry is the review-enforced half of the pair, and that contract file is the single source of truth for approved exceptions.

A change to the design system's type scale or loaded font weights breaks the compliance scan in the app repository, not in this package: the MD3 scale set and the 700 maximum-weight ceiling are constants declared inside the app's scan engine, so the app's unit suite turns red when those package properties move.

The orange (tertiary) usage cap — at most 3–4 elements per screen, with the Grumpy Robot avatar, rating stars, the single "Add movie" call-to-action and attention highlights such as a media/quality mismatch badge as the sanctioned uses — is a convention that the R1–R7 scan does not enforce, so over-using orange is a design regression that will not fail CI.

The design system's own Jest suite uses the `jest-expo` preset with `jest/tamagui-cjs-resolver.js`, which redirects the two Tamagui 3 subpaths whose `react-native` export condition is ESM-only `.mjs` to their CJS builds — a Jest-only problem, since Metro loads `.mjs` fine. `testMatch` covers the whole package rather than only `components/**`, so a new test directory cannot be silently invisible to the runner.

Beyond the rule table, the sanctioned-deviations contract also carries the R1 colour-utility allowlist and the intentional control conventions — two-tier destructive emphasis by surface density and single-select `Chip type="choice"` versus multi-select `Chip type="filter"` — which are documented deliberate differentiation rather than drift.

The orange call-to-action is `PillButton`, a dedicated primitive rather than a `Button` variant because its look sits between the MD3 Button sizes and is semantically singular, and the design system's `FAB` defaults to the tertiary colour scheme — together with `MovieCard`'s `FormatBadge` highlight, these are the sanctioned orange surfaces.

The Tamagui lockstep guard also bounds any Tamagui peer range to the installed major (`>=3.0.0 <4`), requires every `@tamagui/*` entry in the lock to sit at the manifests' one version, and asserts that every Tamagui update resolves to the single `tamagui` Renovate group on patch, minor and major alike. That group rule carries `rangeStrategy: pin` and is deliberately ordered after the broad `js patch/minor` and `js majors` rules, because the last matching `groupName` wins — placed earlier, those pull part of the set back onto its own branch.

The design system's `components/primitives/Text.tsx` also restores the **web** default line height (`lineHeight: web:20px`), because Tamagui 2's stylesheet gave every Tamagui text its font's default (`true`) line height while Tamagui 3 only sets the family — measured as the 22px app-bar title growing 20 → 28px and table rows shrinking 37 → 35px. Native never had that rule, so it is left untouched.

Under Tamagui 3 a numeric `lineHeight` on a Tamagui component is a **ratio**, not pixels; pixel values must be written as a string such as `"20px"`, which is why the design system's `Text` default is a `web:`-scoped string.

Tamagui 3 removed the v2 pseudo-state objects (`hoverStyle` / `pressStyle` / `focusVisibleStyle`): a state is now a clause on the property it modifies, written as a string program (`opacity="hover:0.92 press:0.88"`) or as a key of a typed value. A leftover v2 object still typechecks and is forwarded as an unknown prop, so the interaction silently stops happening. The keyboard-only modifier is `focus-visible`; a bare `focus` clause reproduces the feature-015 bug where a mouse click leaves a persistent focus ring. `components/focus-ring.test.ts` and `components/interaction-states.test.ts` statically assert that no v2 object survives, that every ringed control keeps its `focus-visible` clause, and that `Card`/`Button`/`Chip` each declare hover, press and focus-visible.

The only non-palette colour tokens in the Tamagui config are `white` and `black`; `transparent` is deliberately *not* a token because Tamagui 3 rejects a token named after a CSS keyword and the literal resolves correctly anyway.

The design system's Jest resolver `jest/tamagui-cjs-resolver.js` is wired into the app's own Jest config as well (`frontend/mcm-app/package.json` → `jest.resolver` → `<rootDir>/../../packages/design-system/jest/tamagui-cjs-resolver.js`), so both suites load Tamagui 3 through the same CJS redirect; the resolver's own header names both configs as its callers. The package's `testMatch` was widened from `components/**` to `<rootDir>/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` because a `tokens/` test had been written, committed and never executed, reporting green while testing nothing.

The framework packages this package declares are version-locked to the Expo SDK **repo-wide**, and the lock is asserted against `packages/design-system/package.json` itself, not only the app. The React Native rule disables `react-native`, `/^react-native-/`, `/^@react-native//` and `/^@react-native-community//` with no `matchFileNames` scope, and `scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs` asserts the resolved `enabled` per dependency in each of `package.json`, `frontend/mcm-app/package.json`, `packages/design-system/package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` rather than that a rule mentioning the package exists. The second scope is load-bearing: PR #217 bumped `react-native` 0.85.3 → 0.87.0 through this package's manifest, which the older app-scoped rule could not reach, and RN 0.87 narrowed the press-event type so `GestureResponderEvent` no longer satisfied Tamagui's `PressableProps['onPress']` — 15 typecheck errors across 14 files. The `/^react-native-/` pattern is a second, independent half: it is the only thing covering `react-native-reanimated`, `react-native-worklets`, gesture-handler, screens and safe-area-context, none of which the app-scoped rule matched anywhere. A framework bump in this package therefore goes through `expo install` together with the app, never a raw Renovate bump.

The Expo SDK companion packages are also version-locked repo-wide, by a rule disabling `expo`, `/^expo-/`, `/^@expo//` and `/-expo$/` with no `matchFileNames` scope. This is the third instance of the same scope defect, and the widest: `babel-preset-expo`, `jest-expo` and `eslint-config-expo` carry no `expo` prefix so every pattern in the app-scoped rule missed all three, while `@expo/dom-webview` is declared in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, which a `matchFileNames` rule cannot reach. Measured 2026-08-27 from the Dependency Dashboard (item #29): all four were queued in `js majors` for 56 → 57 while `expo` itself sat at `^56.0.8` and `react-native` was correctly disabled — an SDK-56 runtime against SDK-57 transform and test tooling, which fails as unexplained transform errors rather than as typecheck errors naming a dependency. `@expo-google-fonts/*` is deliberately not matched (`/^@expo//` requires a slash after `@expo`; the font packages separate with a hyphen) and a guard control asserts both font packages still resolve enabled.

The repo-wide version-lock guard is a plain `node:test` file, not part of either Jest suite: `scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs` is executed by the `naming` job's `node --test scripts/__tests__/*.test.mjs` step in `.forgejo/workflows/guardrails.yml`. It resolves `enabled` by replaying the repository's own `packageRules` in order (last matching rule wins, modelled in `scripts/lib/renovate-package-rules.mjs`) and fails loudly on any `match*` form that model does not know. Consequently `pnpm nx test design-system` passing says nothing about the locks, and the `react`/`react-dom`/`react-test-renderer` rule is the one locked family with no per-manifest assertion behind it at all — the guard loops the RN and Expo-companion families only.

The toolchain majors this package shares with the app are held by `dependencyDashboardApproval` rather than by a version ceiling, each in its own group so one dashboard tick releases one blocker: `jest` with `@types/jest` (pinned by jest-expo's jest-29 family at SDK 57, possible at SDK 58) and `typescript` (pinned by typescript-eslint's compiler peer range), both of which name `packages/design-system/package.json` as a declaring manifest. Patch and minor updates are deliberately not matched, so they stay ungated in `js patch/minor`; the `@babel/core`/`@babel/runtime` and `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` holds cover only the app manifest.

`jest/tamagui-cjs-resolver.js` exists because Tamagui 3.0.x maps two subpaths' `react-native` export condition to ESM-only `.mjs` files with no `.native.js` variant — `@tamagui/style-grammar/token-categories`, which `@tamagui/helpers` pulls in and therefore every Tamagui component does, and `@tamagui/core/inject-styles`. Metro loads `.mjs` fine, so the app is unaffected, but Jest treats `.mjs` as native ESM and every suite rendering a Tamagui component failed to run with `Unexpected token 'export'` (56 suites, measured on the 3.0.13 bump). The package's exports map blocks a `moduleNameMapper` to the deep `dist/cjs` path, so the redirect happens in a resolver that delegates to the jest-expo preset's own resolver and rewrites a resolution only when it landed on a Tamagui `dist/esm/*.mjs` whose package also ships the same module at `dist/cjs/*.cjs`, returning the original resolution when that CJS sibling is absent.

The package's Jest config caps its workers at a literal `maxWorkers: 4` with `workerIdleMemoryLimit: '1.5GB'`, and the app's `jest` block carries the same two values. The default is Jest's (cores − 1), which on the 20-vCPU dev sandbox spawned ~19 workers (~0.9 GB each at peak) and let the VM-wide OOM killer take a bystander process — Keycloak's JVM — so the cap is an integer because the constraint is memory rather than core count. `scripts/__tests__/dev-memory-bounds.guard.test.mjs` discovers every git-tracked Jest config (by name, including `packages/design-system/jest.config.js` and `frontend/mcm-app/package.json`) and fails any that sets no literal integer `maxWorkers` of 1–4, or that allows more than one worker without a `workerIdleMemoryLimit`.

MD3 interaction feedback is a state layer rather than an `opacity` change on the element: `tokens/with-alpha.ts` holds the opacities in one place (`stateLayer` = `hover: 0.12`, `focus: 0.14`, `press: 0.18`, deliberately tuned because 8% is invisible on the `#0F1117` dark surface) and `withAlpha(token, alpha)` produces the tint. `withAlpha` exists because the naive `theme.onSurface?.val + '14'` form fails silently two ways: it assumes a 6-digit hex, so a `rgb()`/`hsl()`/named token yields an invalid colour that React Native and the browser both drop without erroring, and the resulting layer was invisible even when valid. It therefore returns a non-hex input unchanged, returns `undefined` for an undefined token, and clamps alpha to 0–1; `tokens/with-alpha.test.ts` pins the non-hex and undefined cases rather than the happy path. Both `withAlpha` and `stateLayer` are exported from the package barrel.

Under Tamagui 3 any state clause — `hover` included — makes a `View` attach its own event handlers on native (`createComponent`'s `shouldAttach` counts a hover program), so a state clause on a Tamagui `View` nested inside an RN `Pressable` makes it the touch responder and swallows the tap: `NavList` and `Tabs` therefore pass their hover layer only when `Platform.OS === 'web'` and put the pressed visual on the outer `Pressable`. The measured symptom is a tap that reports `COMPLETED` to Maestro and then navigates nowhere, which reads as a routing bug; neither the unit tier (`fireEvent.press` targets the `Pressable` directly) nor the web tier (mouse events bubble) can observe it, only Android.

The package suite's contract with the app is behavioural: beyond the success-token, text-defaults and with-alpha tests it covers the focus-ring and interaction-state guards, the controls (`SearchBar`, `Chip`/`ChipGroup`, `Switch`, `Dialog`, `Snackbar`, `Banner`, `Badge`, `Divider`), navigation (`AppBar`, `IconButton`, `NavigationBar`, `Tabs`, `NavList`), the inputs and the domain cards, asserting resolved theme values, rendered style and AA contrast rather than the implementation.

The lockstep guard's instance check is a distinct property from its version check: it counts the distinct `snapshots:` keys per package for `@tamagui/core` and `@tamagui/web` (peer suffix included, since pnpm gives each key its own directory), fails on more than one and names both keys plus `pnpm dedupe`, and fails on **zero** keys too so a parser that stops matching cannot pass vacuously. It reads only the `snapshots:` sections, because pnpm's lock is a multi-document file whose first document carries its own `packages:`/`snapshots:`, and it needs no install because the lock is authoritative.

The instance check exists because one version is not one instance: during the Expo SDK 58 spike `expo install` upgraded only the app, while the design system's devDependencies plus a stale `react-native-safe-area-context@5.7.0` lock entry gave this package a different peer hash, so two `@tamagui/web` instances loaded and every page rendered zero nodes with `Missing theme` — while the export and the API routes both still succeeded, and the version-only guard passed. `pnpm dedupe` is the documented remedy.

`scripts/__tests__/tamagui-version-lockstep.guard.test.mjs` is a plain `node:test` file executed by the `naming` job's `node --test scripts/__tests__/*.test.mjs` step in `.forgejo/workflows/guardrails.yml`, not by either Jest suite, so `pnpm nx test design-system` passing says nothing about the Tamagui lockstep, the Renovate locks, or the app's compliance scan.
